articleTitle: Keynote Speakers and Panel Chairs
abstract: Provides an abstract for each of the keynote presentations and may include a brief professional biography of each presenter. The complete presentations were not made available for publication as part of the conference proceedings.

articleTitle: Factors Influencing Students' Behavioral Intention to Continue Artificial Intelligence Learning
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly employed in education for enhancing teaching practices and meeting students' learning needs. A number of AI learning opportunities in K-12 and higher education continue to grow across the world. Yet, little research has been done to investigate K-12 students' behavioral intention to learn AI. This study, which involved a sample of 131 primary students, examined the factors that affect students' behavioral intention to engage in AI learning. The exploratory factor analysis was employed to validate a four-factor survey. The general factor model includes (i) AI literacy, (ii) confidence in AI, (iii) AI for social good, and (iv) behavioral intention. The results showed that the first 3 factors were positively associated with the last factor. Students perceive the purpose of learning AI for social good as the most powerful predictor for their behavioral intention.

articleTitle: Using a Multiplatform Chatbot as an Online Tutor in a University Course
abstract: Allowing students to ask questions in a university course is a crucial aspect of learning, which leads to increased learning effectiveness but also increased workload of the teaching staff. To reduce their workload, this paper presents the design of a chatbot for instantly answering students' questions on multiple common social platforms including Telegram, Facebook Messenger and Line. The chatbot can answer questions in natural language and commands. Once the teachers upload the necessary course-related information to an online database, the chatbot can answer questions on the course materials and course logistics (e.g., class schedule). The chatbot also supports a login system so as to provide answers according to different student profiles (e.g., schedule of their enrolled class and score dissemination). A survey on ten undergraduate computer science students showed that our chatbot can effectively act as an online tutor to reduce teachers' workload and will be a useful tool to be integrated into other e-learning platforms.

articleTitle: College Students' Autonomous Learning Behavior in Blended Learning: Learning Motivation, Self-Efficacy, and Learning Anxiety
abstract: Blended Learning has changed the traditional teaching mode and attracted wide attention to the educational community. In blended learning, students have more autonomy. This paper aims to study the autonomous learning behavior of college students in blended learning. In this study, five hypotheses were answered by using multiple linear regression. Results show that learning motivation and academic self-efficacy can effectively predict college students' autonomous learning behavior. In addition, academic self-efficacy has a positive effect on learning motivation, and learning anxiety is negatively correlated with learning motivation, learning anxiety and self-efficacy indirectly affect autonomous learning behavior through learning motivation. The results of this study provide new ideas and suggestions for the implementation of blended learning.

Author Keywords: blended learning, autonomous learning behavior, learning motivation, academic self-efficacy, learning anxiety

articleTitle: An IoT Smart Lighting System for University Classrooms
abstract: This research is the development of an IoT based controller device with a cloud-based system to switch, manage, and monitor the lights of university classrooms. The project output shall aid the problem in the operation of lights from unnecessary energy consumption to save energy. The researchers used a NodeMCU V3 with Wi-Fi capabilities together with a Passive-Infrared Sensor to detect room occupancy and a Relay Switch to operate the switching of lights to create the controller device. The controller device can run using the web and mobile applications over the internet using AJAX. The developed applications not only serve as a controller but a management system to set appropriate schedules for class hours, a monitoring system that indicates the length of usage and the total amount of energy consumed from lights. The management can set class schedules to allow the room to operate the lights on a given period if there are occupants in the room. Failure to occupy the room even with a set schedule, the lights will not turn ON, thus reducing excess energy consumption. Furthermore, lights can still be controlled over a separate remote network through the applications even beyond the given schedule.

Author Keywords: Internet of Things, Smart Lighting Systems, Management System, Microcontroller, Sensors

articleTitle: Exploring the Relationships Among Interaction, Emotional Engagement and Learning Persistence in Online Learning Environments
abstract: Learning persistence is recognized as an essential factor for effective online learning, and students interaction and emotional engagement are significant antecedents of learning persistence. In order to promote students' learning achievement and outcome, it is valuable to explore their relationships in online learning environments. Therefore, this study employed structural equation modeling (SEM) to examine the relationships among students' online interaction, emotional engagement and learning persistence. The path model was proposed to test the mediating effects of emotional engagement. Data were collected from 328 university students in China, and the path was analyzed. The results of this study demonstrated that online interaction and emotional engagement were positively associated with students' learning persistence. In addition, emotional engagement also mediated the relationships between student-instructor interaction, student-content interaction and learning persistence in online learning environments. Consequently, from the perspectives of interaction and emotion, implications were discussed to promote students'learning persistence.

Author Keywords: online interaction, learning persistence, emotional engagement, path model

articleTitle: Application of Location-Controlled Mobile Attendance Recording System in College Classroom Teaching
abstract: In the process of college classroom teaching activities, it is necessary to record the attendance of the students. The traditional methods are through the manual way naming statistics, need to take up a lot of time, affecting the normal classroom teaching activities. For the social practice classes, online classrooms, large-scale lectures and other such teaching activities, traditional attendance records methods apparently can't meet the education requirements. In this paper, a mobile attendance record system based position controllable classroom instruction is presented. Students will submit the attendance and location information through the attendance record APP. The teachers can set the attendance location to control the learners must be to the specified location for attendance records or remote attendance records. The experimental results showed that the system is flexible and straightforward, which can save attendance and statistic time, improve teaching efficiency and meet the needs of attendance record in scene teaching activities.

Author Keywords: Location-Controlled, Attendance Record, Classroom Instruction, Smart Terminals, Attendance Recording System

articleTitle: Research on the Influence of College Students' Engagement in Blended Learning: Teacher Support, Situational Interest, and Self-Regulation
abstract: Student engagement is an important indicator to predict students' academic achievements, as well as an important condition to ensure learning quality and promote deep learning. This study investigated the relationship between classroom environment factor (teacher support) and individual factors (situational interest and self-regulation) in blended learning and college students' engagement of specific types (behavioral engagement, cognitive engagement, and emotional engagement). The results show that teacher support and self-regulation have significant influence on college students' behavioral engagement and cognitive engagement. Situational interest and self-regulation have significant influence on college students' emotional engagement. These findings can provide new ideas on improving students' academic achievements and engagement.

Author Keywords: blended learning, student engagement, teacher support, situational interest, self-regulation

articleTitle: Developing a Generic Rubric for Evaluating Students' Work in STEM Education
abstract: Harnessing rubrics in educational assessment is regarded as a promising approach to improving learning and enhancing instructional impact. A well-designed rubric can effectively help communicate expectations of performance to students and provide them with feedback. This study seeks to find an appropriate way to develop a generic rubric that can be adopted by practitioners and researchers to evaluate STEM inventions. In order to secure the validity of the rubric content, we reviewed the literature of (i) rubric design principles, (ii) rubrics in STEM studies, and (iii) rubrics applied in STEM competitions. Based on the review, we proposed that STEM work can be evaluated from six dimensions: (i) problem definition, (ii) feasibility, (iii) usability, (iv) teamwork, (v) entrepreneurship, and (vi) overall presentation and justifications. The present work sheds light on the development of a compatible evaluation tool for STEM learning.

articleTitle: Research and Practice in Smart Learning: A Literature Review
abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of smart learning research and practice published in the past decade (2010-2019). The review includes a total of 85 articles collected from three publication databases, namely Web of Science, Scopus and ProQuest. It covers the patterns of publications on smart learning, the research topics and research purposes, as well as the types of devices/tools and features involved in smart learning practices. Over the period analysed, the results showed an increasing number of publications from a wider range of countries/regions and sources. More than half of the research topics belonged to the categories of smart learning environment and smart classroom. The research purposes most frequently addressed the design and evaluation of smart learning systems/services. The smart learning practices commonly involved the use of mobile and smart devices (e.g. smartphones, tablet computers and sensors), and the features of collaboration, personalisation and intelligence. Based on the results, potential areas for future work are also discussed.

Author Keywords: smart learning, smart education, smart learning environment, smart classroom

articleTitle: Ubiquitous Learning of Renewable Energy and Environmentalism to Various Israeli Populations
abstract: How should children be taught about renewable energy, what is air pollution? This paper reports on a specific case, perception and actual implementation in Hebrew - and Arab - speaking schools in Israel. In the last 4 years students from the HIT, Holon Institute of Technology participated in a course "green ambassadors" which combines practical work. As part of the course requirements, students were asked to conduct enjoyable lessons within the topic of preserving the environment to the pupils in the elementary school. During meetings held within the school, the students taught the pupils via games and activities what renewable energy means, how to turn waste into a resource, what energy conversion and renewable energy mean, etc. In order to illustrate the topics studied by the pupils, the students used a moveable laboratory containing demonstrations, experiments, and creative activities. The results show higher rates of success and involvement due to an enriching and challenging experience of learning. Thanks to all these, the pupils turned more aware and learned an important lesson about the ways to preserve the environment.

Author Keywords: environmental education, experimental learning, elementary school, renewable energy, energy efficiency

articleTitle: Practice Teaching Design and Implementation Based on Kolb's Learning Theory
abstract: Based on the theory of experiential learning and the model of experiential learning cycle proposed by David Kolb, the practical implementation process is constructed. It is proposed that the practical teaching link should be reformed into "diversified training mode based on students' ability and demand", and students should be divided into three directions: scientific research type, innovation and entrepreneurship type and application skill type, and be cultivated in different practical teaching environments according to different training objectives. By adopting various forms of practical teaching mode, students can practice continuously for four years, and the effect of practical teaching is improved.

Author Keywords: teaching, experiential learning, learning cycle theory, internship

articleTitle: Flipped Classroom Approaches in Computer Programming Courses in Japan
abstract: With the rapid development of educational computer software, flipped classrooms have become widely applied in Japanese tertiary educational settings. Through reversing the tradition approach of providing new instructions directly, pre-class online tutorials are believed to bring several effective benefits. For example, expanding students' opportunities to engage in discussions, ask instructors questions, and complete projects in collaboration with their classmates, when they would have otherwise been taking notes during class. This approach is more communicative and learner-centred in that students can take control of their own learning without dependence upon the pacing set by the instructor. Research has been widely conducted into what has come to be known as 'flipped classrooms' across various subjects internationally, although few studies have focused on its efficacy specifically with respect to computer programming. This is particularly true in Japan, where traditional teacher-centred approaches are still widely employed. This study aims to examine the effectiveness of flipped classroom approaches in an undergraduate computer programming course in Japan, with specific attention paid to students' self-reported experiences. The findings reveal an unexpectedly low appreciation of the efficacy of the approach, with the majority of students continuing to prefer in-class paper-based instruction. Students' opinions of the efficacy of pre-learning also varied widely from student to student according to their own preferences, interests, and objectives. These results provide some insight into what should be considered when incorporating these pre-learning materials into one's own flipped-learning classrooms.

Author Keywords: flipped classroom, Japanese students, blended learning, programming

articleTitle: Interactive Contents with 360-Degree Panorama Virtual Reality for Soil and Water Conservation Outdoor Classroom
abstract: The paper proposes an interactive virtual reality (VR) 360-degree panorama application system which can be applied in education for soil and water conservation. In the development of the system, the interactive VR 360-degree panoramic videos are produced first. The contents of videos come from introductions of facilities built in soil and water conservation outdoor classrooms. The design of video contents and interactions between video contents and users is on the basis of the cognitive theory of multimedia learning. Additionally, the system offers an android app developed using VR technology to offer users with interactions between users and videos. Learners first download the app into a smart phone and then insert the phone into a cheap VR helmet. Subsequently, they play the app with wearing the VR helmet to watch VR 360-degree panoramic videos so as to achieve immersion on watching video in a 3D VR environment. Moreover, learners can move the interaction sign, a single-circle shape, by shaking their VR helmets on the specific marks on screen to trigger corresponding interactive actions such as selecting a video, exiting viewing video, answering questions of true-false items, etc. Experimental results show the way participants received the system has better interaction than that without the system. Furthermore, the interaction portfolios are also collected in the cloud space for future analysis. Finally, the system can be also applied in learning activities of performing flipped classroom strategy when people will visit soil and water conservation outdoor classrooms.

Author Keywords: Virtual Reality, 360-degree panoramic video, Multimedia Learning, Cognitive Theory, Soil and Water Conservation

articleTitle: Development of the Motivation and Engagement in Virtual Reality Chinese Language Learning Questionnaire (MEVRCLQ)
abstract: Motivation and engagement play a key role in students' academic achievement. With the increasing adoption of virtual reality (VR) technology in language learning in recent years, there arises an urging need to develop an instrument for assessing the influence of VR technology on students' motivation and engagement in language learning. This research aimed to construct the said instrument, namely Motivational and Engagement in Virtual Reality Chinese Language Learning Questionnaires (MEVRCLQ). With a sample of 196 Chinese secondary school students in Hong Kong, the MEVRCLQ was validated with adequate reliability in measuring students' motivation and engagement in the context of VR-assisted Chinese language learning. This is the first study of investigating the association of students' first language (L1) related learning outcomes with motivation and engagement constructs.

articleTitle: How Multimedia Influence Group Interaction in STEM Education An Epistemic Network Analysis for Online Synchronous Collaborative Learning
abstract: This study is mainly based on epistemic network analysis (ENA), and through the analysis of interactive behaviors of 131 learners in an online collaborative learning environment. Participants came from three classes and they were assigned different multimedia materials (interactive, video and text version) to complete a group worksheet through online discussion. By con-ducting epistemic network analysis, differences between group interaction of three classes were found. it is shown that class using interactive version material communicate more harmoniously and equally with each other, which is in line with the expectation of collaborative learning. Meanwhile, class using text version material formed a negative atmosphere in which members had unequal communication. In the end, we compared ENA to lag sequential analysis (LSA) and discussed the advantages and disadvantages of its application in the field of learning assessment: ENA can avoid the impact of order on the processing of speech data in online synchronous discussions by segmenting conversations by stanza, so as to be a useful supplement to LSA.

Author Keywords: Epistemic Network Analysis, CSCL, STEM Education

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of the Influence of Interactive AR-Based Experiential Teaching on Cognitive Ability in a Chemical Electrolytic Cell Course
abstract: The integration of Augmented Reality (AR) and experiential teaching plays a vital role in teaching practice. This research designs and implements an interactive AR-based experiential course about electrolytic cells in chemistry. The influences are also explored on high school students' cognitive ability, including remembering, understanding and applying dimensions, through classroom comparative experiments. 60 high school students of similar level, who participated in the study, were randomly divided into an experimental group and a control group. The experimental group used an interactive AR program, and the control group used traditional flash animation. The data was collected through pretest, posttest, interviews and questionnaire surveys. The results show that the experimental group performs better on the applying dimension, while the control group performs better on the remembering dimension, and the two groups performs similarly on the understanding dimension. It is concluded that both traditional teaching with flash and AR-based experiential teaching can improve students' cognitive ability. But experiential teaching based on interactive AR can improve students' cognitive ability better on the applying dimension through hands-on practice.

articleTitle: Learner Preparedness in Flipped Classroom: A Case Study of a Flipped Postgraduate Course
abstract: The present study employed a mixed-method research design and gained preliminary understanding of the importance of learner preparedness in a flipped classroom. The program was a master-level quantitative research methodology course, involving a total of 15 students majoring in English Curriculum and Instruction. Data collection involved questionnaires, course artefacts, online quizzes, an end-of-semester exam and post-program interviews. Quantitative results revealed that the students were quite satisfied with the "flip" mode of the course implementation and they also performed well in the end-of-semester exam. On the other hand, qualitative data revealed that pre-class learning and self-regulation are some major challenges for students. Therefore, to improve the effectiveness of the flipped classroom approach, teachers should intentionally integrate intermediate tasks that can facilitate students' self-preparation, i.e., learner preparedness. Also, learning support should be a major concern for administration on the school level to ensure the flip design can work out as expected.

Author Keywords: flipped classroom, learner preparedness, case study, postgraduate course

articleTitle: Curriculum Design with the Integration of STEAM and Educational Game
abstract: With the new curriculum reform goes further in the whole nation and the rapid development of information technology, game-based teaching (or educational game) has gradually become a new hotpot in the research field. This paper designs educational game courses from a comprehensive and cross-cutting angle based on the idea of STEAM education, which is beneficial to the cultivation of college students' problem-solving ability and qualities of innovation. It also provides a new research direction for the cross-research of game education and STEAM education theory.

articleTitle: Does It Matter to Be a Group Leader? Exploring the Impact of Assigned Leadership on Small Group Online Collaborative Learning
abstract: This study investigates the impact of assigned leadership role on learners' participation and learning experience in online collaborative learning. A total of 94 students of an Instructional Design course were randomly assigned into 24 small groups, with 24 group leaders randomly selected from each group. Drawing on learning analytics and self-reports, this study compared six participating behaviors and perceived collaborative learning experiences between group leaders and group members during a 12-week blended course. The findings in general support the effect of assigned leadership on learning participation rather than learning experience. The group leaders exhibited increased participating behaviors such as login, forum view, chat view, and posting when completing highly collaborative learning tasks, but failed to outperform their peer members in less interdependent learning tasks.

Author Keywords: collaborative learning, assigned leadership, participation, learning experience, learning analytics

articleTitle: Factors Affecting Engineering Program Performance using Structural Equation Modeling Technique
abstract: This research aimed to identify factors and factor correlations that affect the efficiency in education of an engineering program. Efficiency in this study was measured by students' GPA and satisfaction of students toward the program. The study was conducted in Thailand, one of the developing countries with a unique culture. The study surveyed the fourth-year industrial engineering students. The data were collected from the Department of Industrial Engineering, Kasetsart University at Bangkhen and Kamphaengsaen campuses. Structural Equation Modeling technique was applied. Exogenous variables were consisted of Teachers, Personal Financial Background, Rules and Regulations of Educational Institutions, Facilities, and School Activities. Endogenous variables were consisted of Activities Participation and Educational Performance. The results showed that 'Teachers' factor was found to be the most impacted factor toward program's satisfaction, followed by school 'Activities'.

articleTitle: Exploring Students' Preferences Toward the Smart Classroom Learning Environment and Academic Performance
abstract: This study explores college students' (n=263) preferences toward the smart classroom learning environment and their academic performances. All students participated in the same course in the smart classroom environment. The data were collected through the Preference Instrument of Smart Classroom Learning Environments and students' final exam. The results of the measurement of environmental preferences show that overall students are fond of the smart classroom environment. Further, the results of the analysis of variance indicate that there are significantly differences in students' preferences for the smart classroom among students in different levels of academic performance. The results reveal a "U" shape in students' academic performances and their preferences on the smart classroom learning environment. The middle-level academic performance students' preference toward the smart classrooms learning environment is notably less than high-level and low-level academic performance students. Based on the findings of this study, suggestions are made for researchers and practitioners.

Author Keywords: Smart classroom, Learning environment preferences, Academic performance

articleTitle: A Digital Educational Game Based on the ARCS Model for Enhancing Information Literacy
abstract: Educational games are normally designed for joyful learning due to its entertaining and educational values. In the present research, we developed a game and applied it in teaching and learning practices. We also discussed the instructional system design model, the educational game design model, and the design and implementation of information literacy game teaching. The results showed that the integration of information literacy curriculums into the digital educational game was effective in promoting learning and could provide some reference values for further research.

articleTitle: Observation of Music Class Teaching in form of Synchronized Interactive Mixed Classroom in Rural Area: A Qualitative Study
abstract: The compulsory education and education equality are interrelated topic in China. The student in the rural area is in various shortage of teaching and learning resources, especially the field of music education. The form of Synchronized Interactive Mixed Classroom brings the music class to the vacancy of teaching sites. Under the situation, this study selects three music lessons as the research subject that applies to the LICC classroom observation evaluation. In view of teacher, student and culture of classroom to analysis the music class teaching and the actuality of music education in rural area.

articleTitle: From PISA 2009 to PISA 2018: Equity in Hong Kong Secondary Mathematics and Science Education
abstract: This study examines equity in mathematics and science education among secondary students in Hong Kong, focusing on the differences of gender, immigration, and family's social-economic status in mathematics and science performance. The analysis involved the datasets extracted from the recent four cycles of Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA): 2009, 2012, 2015, and 2018. Independent sample T-tests and linear regression analyses were conducted. The results showed that: (i) the gender gap was reversed in favour of girls in both mathematics and science in 2018 for the first time since 2009; (ii) native-born students significantly outperformed their immigrant peers in both mathematics and science, but the magnitudes of the differences were small; and (iii) social-economically status had a positive yet modest effect on mathematics and science performance. In a nutshell, Hong Kong secondary students, in general, regardless of immigration status and family's social-economic background, have enjoyed a quality education in mathematics and science, and girls have begun to outperform boys in these two areas.

articleTitle: Eye-Tracking Analysis of Autistic Children's Attention to Social Stimuli
abstract: Autistic children have severe communication and social interaction disorders. With appropriate social stimulating learning materials, game-based e-learning intervention is a new approach to improve social interaction skills of autistic children. At the same time, learning analysis of autistic children is also necessary. In this study, eye-tracking technology was used to analyze the visual attention characteristics of autistic children watching different forms and complexities of social stimuli. 23 autistic children were recruited as research participants, using cartoon and real social stimuli as experimental materials. The multi-factor within-subject design was used. The results showed that autistic children paid more attention to cartoon stimuli than to real stimuli. When the complexity increased, they spent more time looking at the eyes in cartoon stimuli, while the fixation duration in real stimuli became shorter. Autistic children gave priority attention to the mouths rather than the eyes. The results of this research can provide theoretical support for game-based e-learning intervention, and provide guidance for the development of game-based e-learning packages and the design of interventional learning materials.

Author Keywords: autistic children, eye-tracking, visual attention, social stimuli

articleTitle: Research on Connotation of Smart Education
abstract: Nowadays, with the rapid development of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), many countries have been developing Smart Plus vigorously for the sake of enhancing national strength. On account of the development of ICT in education has the trend towards intelligentization, smart education come into being. However, the quality of smart education varies greatly without common definition and connotation analysis of smart education. In the study, the connotation of smart is discussed from perspective of philosophy, Chinese culture, semantics and so forth. Then, expanding the meaning from smart/wisdom to smart education. Furthermore, comparing with the different connotations of smart education which mentioned by researchers both at home and abroad, so as to clean up the border of smart education from technology supporting, data applying and participants to make a contribution to the related research areas.

articleTitle: The Influence of College Students' Continuous Intention to Use Online Course Platform
abstract: The combination of online education and traditional education provides many advantages in higher education. Therefore, many universities offer online elective courses for students to learn online. However, little is known about the learning experience of students after completing the online course. On the basis of the Universal Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), this study attempts to examine college students' continuous intention to use online course platforms through empirical research. Results show that performance expectancy, effort expectancy, facilitating conditions, content quality is positively related to college students' attitude towards online course platforms; Perceived cost and use attitude also is negatively related to students' continuous intention. However, social influence did not affect college students' attitude towards online course platforms. These findings provide new ideas for the design and development of online course platforms.

Author Keywords: college student, UTAUT, continuous intention, online course platform

articleTitle: MOOC-Inside Food Biochemistry Course Blended-Online and Offline Teaching Reform
abstract: This thesis takes the typical basic food biochemistry course in Food Science and Engineering of South China University of Technology (SCUT) as application scenario, and it describes the reform background and implementation process of the blended-online and offline teaching of the MOOC-Inside food biochemistry course. In addition, the effectiveness of this teaching approach is verified from four aspects: students' evaluation, students' achievements in the past four years, students' participation in practical projects and external impact of the course.

articleTitle: The Effect of Thinking Tools on the Argumentation Skills of Pre-Service Science Teachers in Flipped Learning
abstract: The purpose of this study is to explore the impact of the use of thinking tools on the pre-service science teachers' argumentation skills in flipped learning. A single-group repeated experiment involving 34 pre-service science teachers was used. Data about students' argumentation skills and attitudes towards thinking tools was collected. This study found that the students' argumentation skills ranked highest when they used an online collaborative text-based visual thinking tool. The students also preferred to use the text-based visual thinking tool, although they recognized the online collaborative diagram-based thinking tools could better reflect their thinking processes.

Author Keywords: argumentation, thinking tools, flipped classroom, pre-service science teachers

articleTitle: Developing the Descriptively Verbal Skills of Undergraduate Engineering Student by Playing a LEGO Block Building
abstract: Due to the observation of undergraduate engineering students, we have seen some problems in their information communication. This is not an issue of language, but the point is a lack of descriptive story. The audience (information receiver) cannot build the objects or somethings corresponding to the sender's verbal and sometimes it leads to misleading. In this paper, game-based learning using LEGO block building is applied to improve the descriptively verbal skill. The special model, such as a half bird-half dinosaur creature or something that is not a general object, is used as the prototype model. All members of each team cannot see this model except the team leader which will describe the model information to two sub-leaders one by one. The model information will be divided into two parts for each sub-leader which will carry this information to the members of each subgroup. Finally, the finished 3D figure from all teams will be compared with the prototype model. Results show that most of them quite similar to the prototype. However, allowing the opportunity to talk with the team leader again can increase the similarity of the model. This activity can be done in 2-3 hours with 5-10 persons per team.

Author Keywords: LEGO, team management simulation, collaborative learning

articleTitle: The Use of ICT to Promote Learning: A Case Study of a Primary School in Phnom Penh
abstract: The purpose of this study has been to determine the use of ICT to promote learning as a case study of a private primary school in Phnom Penh. The researcher adopted the Sangapac Online Learning (SOL) used to gather information regarding the first-grade students. The researcher used one group pre-test and post-test design of data collection in which 109 students were given the opportunity of participants as test-takers. Inference statistic was used to investigate the result of this modern way of leaning Khmer language in the first-grade students adopted by Sangapac Online Learning as pre-test and post-test. The results indicated the statistically significant difference between pre-test and post-test of the first-grade students. To conclude, the results of this study should be considered in the positive effectiveness on ICT to promote learning of the modern way.

Author Keywords: Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Sangapac Online Learning Platform, Promote Learning, Learning Outcome

articleTitle: Mini-Lectures Interleaved with Exercises Found Beneficial in Online Learning
abstract: Face-to-face classes had been replaced by online classes from primary schools to universities around the world due to COVID-19. In a 4th year computer science course, we forwent conventionally separated lectures and programming laboratories lasting 2 hours each and switched to alternating mini-lectures and student exercises several times in a 2-hour timeslot. Students reported that they learned better with improved motivation in this new class format. Students also indicated that they were mostly neutral about whether the face of professor was shown in online lecture.

Author Keywords: interleaved lecture, mini-lecture, online learning, student motivation, summative assessment, interleaved practice

articleTitle: Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation Theory Applied on Primary Education: Case Study of Czech Teachers
abstract: This paper deals with results of Rogers' Diffusion of Innovation Theory which was applied on Czech primary school teachers. The main objective was to get a deeper insight in teachers' attitudes to innovations, particularly the implementation of ICT into the primary education. Having categorized the respondents (N=167) into groups of Innovators, Early adopters, Early majority, Late majority and Laggards, semi-structured interviews were conducted with two teachers representing each category. Recordings were transcribed and results are presented in the paper. They show higher occurrence of Innovators within the sample, which could work as a strong precondition in further pre-service and in-service teacher training.

Index Terms: Information And Communication Technology In Education
Author Keywords: diffusion, innovator, early adopter, early majority, late majority, laggard

articleTitle: Use Intention of Synchronous Two-Teacher Model: A Study from in-Class Teachers' Perspective
abstract: Based on the universal theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT), this study explores in-class teachers' use intention of the synchronous two-teacher model, which consists of an elite teacher from the well-developed urban school and one or more in-class teachers working together to teaching students at the underdeveloped rural schools. The results show the in-class teachers have a strong welling to participate in the synchronous two-teacher model. Further, the study finds that effort expectancy and facilitating conditions are two factors that have directly impact on in-class teachers' use intention of the synchronous two-teacher model. Performance expectancy and social influence, on the other hand, are two factors that have not directly impact on in-class teachers' use intention of the synchronous two-teacher model.

articleTitle: Effects of Grouping Strategies on Asynchronous Online Discussion: Evidence From Learning Analytics and Social Network Analysis
abstract: Online discussion is an essential element of online instruction and is largely dependent upon its designing and facilitating strategies. To investigate the effects of grouping strategies on asynchronous online discussion, this study conducted a quasi-experimental research design with 178 graduate students to compare the difference in student participation and social interactions between whole-class and small-group discussion, and among groups composed of self-selected acquaintances, partial acquaintances, and randomly-assigned strangers. Based on the statistical results from learning analytics and social network analysis, the findings of this study support the superiority of small discussion groups self-formed by acquaintances, for increased learning participation and social interactions.

Author Keywords: Asynchronous online discussion, group size, group composition, learning analytics, social network analysis

articleTitle: Assessing Intentional Use of AR in Cultural Heritage Learning
abstract: In cultural heritage development, augmented reality (AR) technology plays an essential role, seamlessly realizing immersions by merging virtual objects with real images. It not only combines the virtual and the real, but most importantly, increases overall tourists' interest in culture and history. However, limited research was carried out to explore the determinants of adoption towards AR by potential consumers and to what extent do these factors affect. In this paper, a new research horizon is adopted so as to explain the complex relationship of these influencing factors by using quantitative research. Valid data were collected from participants using a national AR tourism platform in China which was developed on Smart-phones. The main results demonstrate that five variables: Performance Expectancy, Social Influence, Facilitating Conditions, Price Value, and Habit significantly influence the individuals' Behavioral Intention to visit the destination. Personal Innovativeness (PI) moderates Habit (HB) on Behavioral Intention (BI). This novel Augmented Reality (AR) graphic travelling system, which provides not only real environment viewing module, but also live voice guide, stimulates cultural heritage learning.

articleTitle: Research on the Effectiveness of Interactive Learning Activities Based on Rain Classroom
abstract: With the development of informatization teaching, how to effectively use informatization tools to promote the learning effect and improve the learning experience is an urgent problem for teachers. The paper designed interactive learning activities during the whole learning process. It analyses the impact of activities on academic performance. Results showed that there are positive correlations between the number of pages of preview slides and the class exercises score, the class exercises score and the final written test score, the class exercises score and the computer test score. There is no correlation between reading time of preview slides and the class exercises score, neither between the number of barrage and the class exercises score. The interview revealed the advantages of using Rain Classroom to learn, which may provide reference for the teaching reform based on instruction tools.

Author Keywords: Rain Classroom, programming, interactive learning activities, feedback

articleTitle: Exploring the Potential of Virtual Reality for Child Pedestrian Safety Training: A Case Study in China
abstract: This study explores the potential of using virtual reality in conducting child pedestrian safety training by designing and implementing a VR-based training intervention in three elementary schools in China, located in urban, rural, and fringe area respectively. The results suggested enhanced authenticity and interactivity as two technical affordances of VR, which enabled risky behavior diagnosis and personalized remedial instruction. The increased pedestrian performance among children during and after the VR intervention supported its efficacy as an innovative training program. Additionally, the empirical results indicated a limited impact of school location and family SES on children's pedestrian performance, highlighting the need for a universal pedestrian safety training curriculum for elementary schools nationwide.

Author Keywords: virtual reality, pedestrian safety training, efficacy, China, case study

articleTitle: Dual-Teaching Model: A Practical Approach for Students in Rural Areas
abstract: The allocation of educational resources directly affects the realization of educational equity, and teachers are the key resources needed to be allocated. The synchronous model can provide interaction between HTs and students, but the students are limited, and cost much. The asynchronous model is the teaching efficient and cost-effective, but there is no direct interaction between HTs and students. This study proposes a dual-teaching model, which includes HTs from well-developed school districts and LTs from underdeveloped areas working together to complete the entire instructive activities. The model can be divided into three stage include preparation, implementation, and evaluation. HTs are responsible for developing and delivering the main content, LTs provide face-to-face guidance and discussions with students. The preliminary results suggest that DTM has been effective in improving students' learning and in optimizing teachers' resources.

articleTitle: Visual Analysis of the Research and Application of Learning Resource Recommendation System
abstract: With the development of information technology, the learning resource recommendation system as a means of auxiliary teaching has gradually become the research focus of many scholars in the field of education. In this paper, CiteSpace, a visualization software, is used to make a quantitative statistical analysis of journal literature related to the learning resource recommendation system in Web of Science, and four research topics are obtained: recommendation system, collaborative filtering, ontology, and E-learning. This paper summarizes the existing problems and development trends of the study of the learning resource recommendation system.

articleTitle: The Construction and Practice Research of Data-Driven Precision Teaching Model
abstract: The arrival of the data era has brought great changes to education. Data-based teaching aims to promote the improvement of teachers' teaching behaviors through data, thus improving students' academic performance. At present, the popularity of large-scale online learning platforms and the development of data mining and learning analysis technology provide support for the collection and analysis of student data, making data-based precision teaching possible. Based on "smart learning partner", a public service platform for intelligent education developed by Advanced Innovation Center for Future Education of Beijing normal university, this study carried out a research on data-driven precision teaching model, and verified its effectiveness in practical teaching, in the hope of providing theoretical support and practical cases for precision teaching.

articleTitle: Comparations Between Physical and Virtual Manipulatives in Collaborative Inquiry
abstract: The emergence of virtual manipulatives (VM) provides a new possibility for collaborative inquiry learning, which is to combine the interaction between students and digital media resources with the face-to-face communication between group members. Previous researches have investigated the effects of VM in conceptual understanding in science inquiry learning. However, the utility of VM in collaborative inquiry learning remains unclear. Besides, as there is little research on the learning process, we still do not understand the cognitive experience of students when using VM for collaborative inquiry learning. To explore the impact of VM in collaborative inquiry learning on both the learning outcome and the learning process, this study was designed to compare the effects of physical manipulatives (PM) and VM from students' performance level and cognitive level in an authentic class. For performance level, we examined both the instant group learning results and individual long-term knowledge retention. For cognitive level, we investigated the cognitive load and task involvement of the students. In this study, we conducted a quasi-experiment and distributed the cognitive load scale. 53 primary students in two comparable classes participated in the study. The findings indicated that students using VM perform better both in instant group results and individual knowledge retention than the students interacting with PM. As for the cognitive level, students using VM also reported a higher level of task involvement.

articleTitle: Research on the Satisfaction of Kid's English Education Application Based on Importance-Performance Analysis (IPA)
abstract: In this study, the English education app for kids is defined as a third-party application developed for kid's online English learning. In order to enhance its competitiveness, this study analyzed mainly four parts of it: Education pattern, Subject content, Teaching methods and Teaching scenarios. The empirical results were obtained in a sample of 141 parents in China. The final result of Importance - Performance Analysis in this study provides implications for developers to improve the English education app that encourages the kids to learn English more effectively.

Author Keywords: English education application, important performance analysis, satisfaction

articleTitle: The Difference Evaluation of the ICT Competency to University Teachers from Two Perspectives in the Era of Mobile Internet
abstract: In the era of mobile Internet, the combination of information technology and teaching activities is increasingly close, and information technology means are increasingly rich. The competency of teachers" Information and Communications Technology (ICT) has become a necessary condition in the teaching process, and how to evaluate it accurately is the key problem. For teachers" ICT evaluation, however, there are significant differences between students and teachers. According to the two-dimensional analysis framework based on 7D4L, this paper carries out a questionnaire research. Based on the specific framework content of 28 modules in the evaluation system of teachers" ICT competency, two sets of questionnaires based on teachers" and students" perspectives are designed. The evaluation of teachers" ICT competency is carried out from the subjective and objective perspectives, and the differentiation problem is studied through the differential evaluation between students and teachers. Through the comparative study of the results of the questionnaire, this paper analyzes the causes and effects of the conclusions of consistency and difference. Finally, the main strategies to improve teachers" ICT competency are put forward.

articleTitle: English Language Development via Erasmus+: Students' Feedback
abstract: This paper deals with students' feedback on their English language development after the one semester long stay at the Czech university within Erasmus+ Exchange programme. They expressed opinions on improving their language skills. Two questionnaires were administered by 83 Erasmus+ Exchange students from five countries after arrival and before departure. Each questionnaire consisted of ten statements evaluated on the four-level Likert scale. Results showed improved speaking skills, minimized anxiety and higher level of self-confidence and self-belief in most respondents.

Author Keywords: Erasmus Exchange programme, English language, students'feedback

articleTitle: Attention-Based CNN for Personalized Course Recommendations for MOOC Learners
abstract: Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), which are open for anyone without limitations on time or location, have attracted millions of registered online students. The large number of online courses available raises the question of how appropriate courses can be effectively recommended to interested learners. The recommendation system, widely used in various online applications, is a good solution for reducing decision complexity. In this paper, we propose the method of using attention-based convolutional neural networks (CNN) to obtain a user's profile, predict the user ratings, and recommend the top-n courses. First, we represent the learner behaviors and learning histories into feature vectors. The attention mechanism is then used to improve relevance estimation according to the differences between the estimation scores and the actual scores given by users to train the neural network. Finally, the trained model will recommend courses to learners. At the end of the paper, we introduce the framework of our system.

articleTitle: Conceptual Assessment Framework of Students' Information Literacy: An Evidence-Centered Design Approach
abstract: This study proposed a conceptual assessment framework of students' information literacy based on the Evidence-Centered Design (ECD) model. Firstly, student model was designed to describe the relevant variables of knowledge, skills and abilities to be measured in terms of students' information literacy. Secondly, evidence model was presented, including the evidence rules and measurement model of students' information literacy. Thirdly, task model was proposed to describe various kinds of tasks in order to obtain the evidence needed by the evidence model. Then, the implementation of students' information literacy assessment based on the ECD model was introduced. Finally, the authors proposed future studies regarding with empirical research on students' information literacy assessment based on the ECD model.

Author Keywords: information literacy, students, conceptual assessment framework, Evidence-Centered Design (ECD)

articleTitle: The Development and Effect Analysis of the Deep-Learning Classroom Model of Primary School Mathematics in the Intelligent Environment
abstract: Mathematics, which is a fundamental subject to cultivate students' high-level thinking ability, lays sound foundation for students to adapt the rapid development of society. The recent growth of intelligent technologies contributes to the revolution of primary school mathematics teaching. This study com-bines the general deep learning model and the primary school mathematics teaching process. Literature research, theoretical deduction, action research, and quasiexperimental research methods are conducted to develop the primary school mathematics deep-learning classroom model within the intelligent environment. Moreover, we applied the model in teaching practice in a Guangzhou Smart-Campus project pilot school to validate the model. The results indicated that the deep-learning classroom model of primary school mathematics could effectively promote the development of math Core Literacy, improve students' academic performance, and cultivate students' knowledge transfer and problem-solving ability.

Author Keywords: Intelligent Environment, Primary School Mathematics, Deep-learning Class-room Model, Effectiveness Evaluation

articleTitle: On the Study of Digital Learning Interactive Method in Situated Learning
abstract: The digital learning has been an important subject for improvement and research in education, especially the development of the Internet and the advancement of computer multimedia tools. This study involves the design of teaching materials and how the role of the teacher acts in digital teaching videos. Thus, two teaching methods are concerned to capture the teaching videos, one is only to capture teaching screen (PPT) without teacher's body language, and the other is to capture teacher's presentation in front of an interactive whiteboard such that the teacher can reveal the situation of problem-solving and logical thinking. Contributions of this research are clearly to state "Teaching Material Favorability" and "Learning Motivation" which will really allow students to cause accompanied effect and reflection in their learning interest from situated impacts.

Author Keywords: digital learning, learning interactive, situated Learning, e-Learning, Multimedia Learning

articleTitle: A Collaborative Model of Blended Learning for the Cultivation of Qualified Pre-Service English Teachers
abstract: A collaborative model of blended learning which includes practices such as online/offline English learning, task-driven coordination, and on/off-site tutoring has been established and successfully implemented with Chinese college students of English education major. By having English language courses, English education module courses by way of face-to-face instruction and self-paced online learning, students greatly enhanced their English skills and pedagogic knowledge. By receiving online/offline supervision both from university teachers and experienced teachers of primary and secondary schools, students enhanced their practical English teaching skills.

articleTitle: A Meta-Analysis of Students' Cognitive Learning Outcomes in Smart Classroom-Based Instruction
abstract: The findings of previous research on the effectiveness of smart classroom-based instructions on student learning outcomes are mixed. The purpose of the present study was to identify high-quality empirical publications that examine the learning outcomes of students and to utilize meta-analyses to determine the overall effectiveness of smart classroom-based instructions. A total of 21 studies were included in this systematic review. The calculated effect size showed that smart classroom-based instructions can positively influence students' cognitive learning outcomes compared to traditional lectures. Moderator variable analysis suggests that the sample size significantly moderates the effectiveness of smart classroom-based classroom instruction. These results indicate that the smart classroom-based instructional model can be an effective approach, especially in large courses.

articleTitle: The Exploration and Practice of IT Solutions for Online Classes in Higher Education During COVID-19 Pandemic
abstract: Due to the COVID-19, the Ministry of Education of China announced that the 2020 spring semester will be postponed, on-site classes should be cancelled and schools should give online classes instead. It's the first time that online classes have been given priority to higher education, which is a new challenge to both schools and online learning platforms. It's necessary to carry out stable and efficient IT solutions to secure the smooth process of online classes. This paper takes South China University of Technology as an example to put forward some IT solutions and ways of improving teaching quality of online classes for higher education during COVID-19 pandemic.

Author Keywords: IT Solution, Online Class, Online Teaching Platform, COVID-19 Pandemic, MOOC

articleTitle: An Online Personality Traits Mining Approach Based on Cluster Analysis
abstract: Mining personality traits online plays an important role in obtaining user personality characteristics, which can indirectly affect online behavior, especially in online learning context. However, traditional researches on personality traits are mainly based on self-assessment, with the disadvantages of being subjective, not scalable and requiring lots of workload. This paper proposed an online personality traits mining approach on Sina microblog social platform by using Gaussian Mixture Model algorithm for data mining and cluster analysis. Through analysis and comparison of online user text features and behavioral characteristics, a 14-cluster personality traits model was constructed and unified in the Big Five-Factor Model by quantifying the correlation between personality traits and characteristics. With the advantages of accuracy, objectivity and strong scalability, the approach proposed in this paper provides new ideas for online personality traits mining and can be used in multiple application scenarios.

Author Keywords: cluster analysis, online personality traits, data mining

articleTitle: A Sense of Fulfillment or Inevitable Stress? Unraveling the Phenomenon of Teacher Anxiety in Synchronous Online Classroom for Rural Education
abstract: Synchronous online classrooms are perceived as an effective approach to promote education equity. But it also brings challenges to teachers and students because of the technical limitations. The present study is a qualitative inquiry into the teacher experience and feelings, especially the negative feelings such as stress and anxiety, through in-depth interviews with nine teachers teaching synchronous online classroom in rural China. The findings revealed that teachers' emotional responses in synchronous online classrooms are highly relevant with teachers' perceptions and expectation of student behaviors, and the teachers' long-term emotional response may be affected by the emotional labor experienced in daily teaching practice in online classrooms. Teacher culture and the changing role of teachers in online instructional contexts can also affect teachers' emotional experience. The research findings contribute to the theory of teacher emotions and can also inform the school administrators and policymakers regarding the potential challenge facing teachers in synchronous online classrooms.

articleTitle: Improving College Students' English Writing Performance via Vlog
abstract: With the development of EFL (English as a Foreign Language) writing research, an effective writing process of EFL learners should involve functions of process writing, teacher's instruction, peers' interaction and collaboration. Process-oriented writing, focusing on the writing process, emphasizes interactivity and revision with teachers' guidance. Meanwhile, SNS (Social Networking Services) tools such as Tencent Instance Messenger (TIM) and vlog have the advantage of strong interactivity and the potential of improving cooperation among learners. This study carried out an experimental research applying vlog group activities inside and outside English writing class, with the aim of investigating its effect on learners' writing performance. 99 freshmen and 101 sophomores were recruited and positive improvements had been observed in lexical complexity and total scores among experimental group members. A survey about learners' perceptions and attitudes towards vlog application in writing was also conducted among 91 learners in vlog group. Most learners viewed vlog as an enjoyable and effective way to advance their writing performance. In conclusion, the results of this study showed that improvement could be seen in both groups' writing performance from pretest to posttest, but the average total score of the experimental group was significantly higher. And progresses in lexical complexity could only be witnessed in the experimental group.

Author Keywords: possess-oriented writing, vlog, writing performance, English writing

articleTitle: Assessing the Effectiveness of Virtual Reality Courseware for Experiential Learning
abstract: Virtual Reality technology brings immersive learning experience to learners in a limited learning environment by restoring real situations as much as possible. It provides conditions for experiential learning. Experiential learning means that students actively construct knowledge from experience, which has the advantages of high participation and enthusiasm, and has gradually become the focus of research in the field of education. Our research adopts an experimental design method. From the perspective of adult higher education, 27 adult learners from Shanghai Open University were selected to carry out an experiential learning activity experiment based on Virtual Reality courseware. The experiment takes learning satisfaction and behavioral willingness as indicators of experiential learning behavior. Investigate the effectiveness of Virtual Reality courseware for experiential learning. The experiment finally revealed that the learning ability of learners and the perceived pleasure of learning content have a significant positive impact on learning satisfaction, and technology perceived ease of use and technology perceived usefulness have a positive impact on the behavioral willingness.

articleTitle: Analysis of Informatics as a New Subject with the New Approach in Elementary and Secondary Education
abstract: This study aims to examine whether the Informatics subject has good quality in terms of content and the readiness of schools and teachers. The paper uses a qualitative research method and discusses the availability of the material and the preparation of schools to use the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) method in the Informatics as the new subject. STEM is a solution to encourage students to have skills that are suitable for the needs of the workplace today. The researcher collected the data using the literature study method, as well as the distribution of questionnaires and interviews with school leaders. This research shows that the content of the subject can meet STEM standards. Also, schools are ready to implement the Informatics in terms of system, teachers, and facilities. However, the government that launched the concept and asked the schools to implement the idea didn't support the school well and tended to push the autonomy of schools.

Author Keywords: Technology 4.0, curriculum, STEM, higher-order thinking skills (HOTS), problem solving

articleTitle: The Basic Concept and Sector Model of Educational Behavior Data
abstract: With the innovative integration of technology and industry represented by artificial intelligence, big data, blockchain, informatization has become the basic power to promote social development. The development of education informatization has become an important part of the sustainable development of information society. With the gradual promotion of educational informatization, a lot of data has been accumulated, which provides more possibilities for educational evaluation. People pay more attention to the concepts of educational data, big data, learning data, learning process. However, people lack systematic understanding of concept connotation, application objectives, analysis methods. Based on this, we propose the basic concept and factor model of educational behavior data. Data, purpose, method, object (3W1H) are four important factors of educational behavior data, which are linked and interact with each other. The inner and outer cycle show two ways for practical application of educational behavior data, which indicates that the concept of educational behavior data is the product of the times with the development of technology.

Author Keywords: Educational behavior data, Concept, Sector model

articleTitle: The Cognitive Diagnosis Based on the Framework of Junior High School Mathematics Knowledge and Ability
abstract: With challenges of the traditional "only fractional" in educational assessment, researchers have been paying more and more attention to the intelligent diagnosis and assessment of disciplines, so there are many intelligent assessment systems for students now. However, there are less researches focusing on the studies of special discipline characteristics, such as skills and ability in China. In this paper, we have established a multi-dimensional framework of mathematical knowledge ability attributes and applied it to the Mathematical Diagnostic System (MDS-KA) to help students develop comprehensively. First, the framework of mathematical knowledge ability attributes diagnoses students' cognitive structure from the three dimensions of knowledge, skills and abilities, and accurately locates students' weak points. Second, the MDS-KA system is integrated into the above framework, intelligently assesses students' learning situation, and combine with empirical research to explore the effectiveness of the framework and system. By the analysis of feedback questionnaire data, there were more than 87% of students think that the individual diagnosis report is consistent with their real learning situation and helpful for learning.

Author Keywords: the framework of knowledge and ability
subject diagnosis system of knowledge and ability

articleTitle: Educational Project #Betterrefs - Possibilities of using Technologies to Maintain Basketball Referees' Performance During Season Interruption: A Pilot Study
abstract: Basketball season was interrupted in March 2020, similarly as other sports competitions, due to the social distancing measures aimed at minimising the spread of coronavirus infection. The interruption might be much longer than common off-season and searching for the possible ways to prevent the athletes from decrease in performance is needed. The educational project #Betterrefs aims to help to maintain the level of the selected components of the referee's performance (knowledge of basketball rules and their interpretations, decision-making skills to judge game situations and players' actions, and physical preparation). The 4 week pilot study comprised all the referees (n = 165) of the Czech Association of Basketball Referees (CABR). The aim was to find out how the #Betterrefs project works in practice, and describe the interest and involvement of the referees. The results showed lower interest among the younger referees (16 - 30) compared to the other age categories (31 years and older), with regard to the age distribution of the basic sample. The highest interest was found in the video-test (98%) and in the rules test (94%), while only 31% of the referees got involved in the physical training. It is expected that this educational project would be in use throughout the whole period of the interruption of basketball competitions in the Czech Republic.

articleTitle: An Empirical Study on Users' Intention to Pay in B2C Online Education Platform
abstract: Online education has been developing since the 1990s, and many traditional education institutions have begun to explore online education development models. Therefore, this paper aims to study the new profit model of B2C online education and improve user stickiness and intention to pay, promoting the healthy development of B2C online education platforms. This paper uses a combination of structural equation model and artificial neural network prediction to conduct empirical research. 557 valid questionnaires were collected, and data analysis was performed using SPSS24.0 and Amos22.0. The research results show that perceived utilitarian value, Word-of-Mouth, and personalization have a positive effect on MOOC continuance intention, which then have a positive effect on willingness to pay with perceived price fairness. The innovation of this research is to build a structural equation model by reading the literature, and then combine it with artificial neural network methods. Few scholars in the field of B2C online education used two empirical methods. The research of this paper is specifically targeted at B2C online education companies, and the results have important guiding effects in this field.
